blocks.text: NMR spectroscopy is based on the magnetic property (nuclear spin) of some nuclei. Nuclei such as hydrogen (1H) and carbon-13 (13C) behave like tiny magnets. With no magnetic field, all such nuclei point randomly and have the same energy. In a strong magnetic field they line up either with the field or against it, giving two spin states: a lower-energy state and a higher-energy state.

blocks.alt: Energy axis pointing up. On the left, two spinning nuclei, one with its arrow up and one with its arrow down, sit on one energy level, labelled before field is applied. The level then splits into two: an upper level labelled 'against' with a nucleus whose arrow points down, and a lower level labelled 'with' with a nucleus whose arrow points up; a double-headed arrow joins the two levels. Label: after field is applied.
blocks.caption: Figure 30.1: Alignment of nuclei in a magnetic field and spin flipping (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 30.1).

blocks.text: Radio waves of the right energy make nuclei in the lower state absorb energy and move to the higher state (spin flipping). When they return they give out energy, which is detected and turned into an NMR spectrum. The exact energy needed to flip a nucleus depends on its position in the compound and the atoms around it, together called its molecular environment. So NMR can tell apart hydrogen atoms in different environments in one molecule: in methanol, CH3OH, the three hydrogens on carbon and the one on oxygen absorb different energies. In practice, nuclei in different environments can be flipped with radio waves of a fixed frequency by varying the strength of the magnetic field.

blocks.alt: Displayed formula of methanol: a carbon atom bonded to three hydrogen atoms (blue) and to an oxygen atom, which is bonded to one hydrogen atom (red). Label: methanol.
blocks.caption: Methanol (original drawing after the structure printed at the end of 30.1).

blocks.title: Did you know?
blocks.text: Nuclei with even numbers of both protons and neutrons, such as 12C, have their nuclear spins paired, so they have no overall magnetic field and give no NMR signal.
